data.description:
## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, authorized at full scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.
This is deliverable 5.

## Independent

Touches the rebar-implement workflow's close phase. No shared file with the criteria
stories, so it can run in parallel with them.

## The gap

Two kinds of artifact are created DURING implementation on the understanding that they are
temporary, and nothing ever removes them.

1. **Held-out twins.** The rebar-implement convention writes a held-out twin test
   alongside the implementation. There is no merge step, so the twin survives. 88 of them
   accumulated and were deleted wholesale by the complexity-reduction program.

2. **Seam-guard modules.** A module-size-cap split produces a guard test asserting the
   split's shape. Once the split has landed and settled, the guard pins refactor mechanics
   and nothing else. Four such modules accumulated from split commits on 2026-07-30,
   08-13, and 08-19.

Both are gate-induced: the process that creates them is the process that is supposed to be
improving the code. Neither has an owner at close time because the epic that created them
closes without looking.

## The change

Move both cleanups into rebar-implement's epic CLOSE phase. At close:

- held-out twins created under the epic are merged into their counterpart test modules
- seam-guard modules created by the epic's split commits are deleted

The close phase is the right home because it is the first moment the full set of artifacts
an epic created is knowable. Doing it per-story would be premature — a twin may still be
serving a sibling story.

## Relationship to the test-taxonomy story

`f86e-b57b-008d-4652` makes the code-review gate ASK about mechanics-pinning tests at
review time. This story REMOVES the ones the workflow itself generates, at close time.
They address the same class from opposite ends and neither subsumes the other: the gate
cannot delete an artifact, and the close phase cannot catch a hand-written one.

## Portability

Per `project.portability`, a capability whose only trigger is a specific CI system is not
portable. The close phase is operation-linked — it runs as part of the epic close, which
is a rebar operation with no CI dependency. The plan must state that explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The rebar-implement workflow has a documented close phase that merges held-out twins
      created under the epic. Verified by reading the workflow definition and by a test
      asserting the phase is present.
- [ ] The close phase deletes seam-guard modules created by the epic's split commits.
      Verified by a test.
- [ ] A twin whose counterpart module does not exist is reported rather than silently
      dropped. Verified by a test, so the merge cannot lose a test.
- [ ] A seam guard NOT created by this epic is left untouched. Verified by a test, so the
      deletion is proven scoped.
- [ ] Closing an epic that created neither artifact completes unchanged. Verified by a
      test, so the close phase is proven inert on ordinary epics.
- [ ] The close phase runs with no CI provider present. Verified by a test that exercises
      it with no CI environment configured.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Plan grounding

Exact file:line citations for the rebar-implement workflow definition, its close phase (or
the absence of one), the held-out twin naming convention, and the seam-guard module
naming convention are being measured against `origin/main` and will be written into this
description before plan review is requested. This ticket is NOT ready for review until
that is done.
data.title: Move held-out twin merging and seam-guard deletion into rebar-implement's epic close phase
